This guard checks the stored label and does not rehash an archive or installed package.
./docs/USAGE.md:33:`add` downloads an npm artifact, verifies its registry integrity, and indexes its TypeScript APIs without running package lifecycle scripts. It does not add a dependency to your workspace. Search uses that local index after preparation, including when offline.
./docs/USAGE.md:144:`sync` indexes direct locked dependencies, including development and optional dependencies. Supply package names to restrict it, for example `typelatch sync kysely`. Packages without usable TypeScript evidence are reported as `unsupported`, and synchronization continues for the remaining dependencies. ./docs/USAGE.md:155:Workspace packages can use a lockfile in a parent directory. Aliases retain the actual registry package name. Lockfile discovery works in JavaScript projects without a `tsconfig.json`. This does not change the TypeScript evidence required for package API indexing.
./docs/USAGE.md:161:Deno projects can declare npm imports in `deno.json` or `deno.jsonc`, including aliases and import subpaths. Declared Deno workspace members, inherited root imports and saved project selections are supported. Package API indexing covers exact npm entries with recorded integrity, using the [Deno lockfile formats](https://github.com/denoland/deno/tree/main/libs/lockfile). JSR packages, remote modules, npm tarball overrides, external import maps, scoped import maps, links, vendored resolution, disabled locking and custom lockfile paths produce explicit limitations. Typelatch does not run the Deno compiler or index JSR package APIs. Schema 1 contained remote module hashes and is not supported for npm API indexing.
./docs/USAGE.md:163:An explicit npm or Yarn Classic artifact URL must identify the canonical package and version tarball on `registry.npmjs.org` or `registry.yarnpkg.com`, or carry an integrity value that must match registry metadata when downloaded. Custom URLs without that evidence are rejected. Legacy canonical URLs with a SHA1 fragment retain registry identity; that fragment is not promoted to a separately verified integrity field.
./docs/USAGE.md:205:Each project uses its nearest applicable lockfile. Independent nested projects can use different package managers. The complete plan is checked before downloads begin. Identical package artifacts are indexed once; different versions are retained. Conflicting integrity values for the same package and version stop sync because one cache entry cannot represent both artifacts.
./docs/USAGE.md:209:Malformed files, unknown schemas and unresolved direct registry identities produce errors. Local workspace, file and link declarations are not downloaded by `sync` as registry packages. Git, patched and repaired package entries are not represented as unchanged registry artifacts. A binary `bun.lockb` containing patch records requires conversion to text because Bun's Yarn printer does not retain those records. Without Bun on `PATH`, convert the binary lockfile with `bun install --save-text-lockfile --frozen-lockfile --lockfile-only` before using Typelatch.
./docs/USAGE.md:248:Both tools validate managed index metadata before returning evidence. Stored package and version must match the requested identity, and stored artifact integrity must be nonblank. An identity mismatch or incomplete metadata returns `Brain metadata does not match name@version. Rebuild: typelatch add name@version`. Valid older index formats remain readable without rebuilding. This check protects the cache label; it does not revalidate the registry archive or establish that installed package files match it.
./docs/USAGE.md:302:Search discovers nested package manifests, TypeScript configs, installed dependencies and nested transitive installations. It uses each installed manifest's name and exact version, including aliases and multiple versions, rather than the newest global index. Supported npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun text lockfiles also provide exact candidates when packages are not installed. These results are labeled `identity: "lockfile"` and `installed: false`. A lockfile candidate is not proof of workspace resolution. Unsupported formats and resolutions are reported as coverage gaps; available installed manifests can still supply identities. For lock entries without an installation path, dependency roots point to the lockfile. Modern Yarn checksums describe Yarn archives and are not treated as npm artifact integrity. Unidentified declared dependencies are reported.
./docs/USAGE.md:304:Search uses existing package indexes and does not download or build missing ones. Run `typelatch sync --workspaces` for declared workspace packages, or select projects with repeated `--project` flags, to prepare their direct locked dependencies. Missing entries in `coverage.dependencies` include exact `typelatch add name@version` commands, including for transitive packages. A JavaScript package without usable TypeScript declarations may still be unindexable. Do not substitute another version. Registry metadata and any available lockfile integrity must match; installed artifact equivalence remains unknown.
./docs/USAGE.md:306:Each source hit includes an absolute `source`, `line`, `endLine`, compact `snippet`, owning `projectRoot`, and optional `symbol` and `position`. A dependency hit instead identifies its package, exact version, registry integrity, artifact relative source path, and known dependency roots. Inspect it with `library_symbol` using that identity. `coverage.configs` lists discovered configs; the agent must select one that owns the relevant file before using `workspace_context`.
./docs/USAGE.md:368:`expectedVersion` checks the package containing the resolved declaration. When declarations come from a separate `@types` package, that identity can differ from the runtime package. A matching version is not proof that installed files equal the registry artifact.
./docs/USAGE.md:404:Results keep `pass`, `fail`, `unknown`, and `not-run` distinct. A command returning zero establishes only the assertions it actually ran. `artifactMatch` remains `unknown` when installed contents have not been compared with the registry artifact.

If several package managers have lockfiles, set `packageManager` in `package.json` to choose one. npm shrinkwrap takes precedence for legacy npm; an explicit `npm@12` or newer selects `package-lock.json` because [npm 12 no longer reads shrinkwrap](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/configuring-npm/package-lock-json/#npm-shrinkwrapjson). Bun text takes precedence over Bun binary. Binary reading uses [Bun's lockfile printer](https://bun.sh/guides/install/yarnlock) on a temporary copy of the observed bytes. It does not install dependencies or run lifecycle scripts.

pnpm and Bun catalogs use the exact resolved entries in the lockfile. Binary Bun catalog aliases also use catalog declarations from the root `package.json` to recover the package name omitted by the printer. Yarn catalogs use the root `.yarnrc.yml` catalog declarations to select the matching locked descriptor. Missing catalog entries or descriptors remain unresolved; Typelatch never chooses a version from a catalog range. Unrelated Yarn configuration fields are not retained as catalog evidence.

Deno projects can declare npm imports in `deno.json` or `deno.jsonc`, including aliases and import subpaths. Declared Deno workspace members, inherited root imports and saved project selections are supported. Package API indexing covers exact npm entries with recorded integrity, using the [Deno lockfile formats](https://github.com/denoland/deno/tree/main/libs/lockfile). JSR packages, remote modules, npm tarball overrides, external import maps, scoped import maps, links, vendored resolution, disabled locking and custom lockfile paths produce explicit limitations. Typelatch does not run the Deno compiler or index JSR package APIs. Schema 1 contained remote module hashes and is not supported for npm API indexing.

An explicit npm or Yarn Classic artifact URL must identify the canonical package and version tarball on `registry.npmjs.org` or `registry.yarnpkg.com`, or carry an integrity value that must match registry metadata when downloaded. Custom URLs without that evidence are rejected. Legacy canonical URLs with a SHA1 fragment retain registry identity; that fragment is not promoted to a separately verified integrity field.

Workspace and dependency candidates receive a shared lexical score based on content, rather than comparing the existing package rank numbers. Results expose bounded retrieval, inventory gaps, exact locations, and separate evidence states. CLI and MCP discovery run in a separate `search-worker.ts` process through the existing bounded worker queue, so synchronous indexing cannot block the server from enforcing cancellation and deadlines. The existing workspace context and validation paths remain responsible for compiler and execution evidence. Workspace cache transactions keep index refresh and candidate selection together; the filesystem reads themselves are not an atomic snapshot.

Workspace cache schema 6 stores excerpt offsets and lengths and refers to file paths by numeric identity. A contentless FTS index holds search postings without storing excerpt text. Search reconstructs excerpts from the same content inventory whose hashes were checked for that request, including unchanged files. Older caches rebuild from current file contents and reclaim obsolete pages. File content hashes, ranking weights, candidate limits and source locations retain their existing meaning.

New empty caches use 1024 byte pages when the inventory contains at most 32 searchable files and 64 KiB of UTF8 text. Larger new caches use the SQLite default. Existing caches retain their page size through growth or contraction. This reduces initial small cache overhead without changing FTS detail or retrieval. It adds no recurring VACUUM operation. A formerly small cache can cost more space after substantial growth; the recorded experiment quantifies that tradeoff.

`workspace/source-context.ts` projects optional source context from that same inventory. It deduplicates selected files, finds direct literal relative imports in source syntax and includes only unambiguous candidates already inside the selected inventory. It performs no file reads or compiler resolution. Source text and file counts have fixed bounds, with hashes, line ranges and omissions exposed to callers. Full and compact search behavior remain unchanged.

Pass those fields to `workspace_context`, or use the CLI:

```sh
typelatch workspace context.json
```

For a known installed export, supply `importSpecifier` and its exact `symbol` path, such as `Schema.Struct`. Omit `question` and `position` to use the `installed-api` route without preparing a package index. Context uses the project's installed TypeScript compiler and returns resolved dependency identity and API evidence. It does not compile the project or run tests.

`api.type` and `api.signatures` are compiler formatted and can include inference. Signatures use the callable value when a declaration also defines an interface. `api.evidence.declarations.headers` separately returns normalized declared syntax, source positions and hashes of the compiler source text. Headers omit implementation bodies, class and namespace members, and unsupported variable initializers. They preserve declared annotations rather than inventing return types. Each header exposes its elisions and `complete`, `truncated` or `unsupported` status. Here `complete` means complete under this elision policy. An unsupported header has a reason and no header text. Older project compilers can still return resolved types and signatures; when their modifier or declaration factory APIs cannot support normalized headers, that projection reports `unsupported` with a reason.

`api.evidence` records total, returned and omitted counts. Text counts use UTF16 code units. Existing limits are 16000 for the type, 12000 for documentation, ten signatures of 8000 each, and ten declaration spans. Additional evidence contains up to ten headers of 8000 each and ten compiler JSDoc tags, with 256 units per name and 4000 per tag text. Documentation and tags are compiler views, not full package documentation or an API graph. These richer responses have a payload cost; preparing no index does not imply lower query memory or latency.

## MCP tool reference

| Tool | Request | Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `workspace_search` | absolute `workspaceRoot`, `question`; optional `scope`, `file`, `detail`, `limit` from 1 to 20, `timeoutMs` | Ranked local file and exact dependency candidates, cache refresh details, coverage and evidence limits |
| `library_search` | `package`, `question`; optional `version`, `limit` from 1 to 20 | Search results from an installed index |
| `library_symbol` | `package`, `symbol`; optional `version` | Exact symbol lookup and relationships |
| `workspace_context` | `config`, `file`; optional `importSpecifier`, `symbol`, `position`, `question`, `expectedVersion`, `overlays`, `limit`, `timeoutMs` | Workspace definitions, types, identity, and optional discovery |
| `workspace_validate` | `config`; optional `testCommand`, `queryId`, `record`, `overlays`, `timeoutMs`, `runtimeInputs`, `snapshotExclude`, `workspaceRoot` | Compiler, execution, and input stability evidence |
| `library_feedback` | `queryId` UUID; optional `accepted`, `compilePassed`, `testsPassed`, `notes` up to 1000 characters | Agent reported outcome stored against a prior query |
| `library_stats` | `{}` | Local query, latency, hit rate, context size, and outcome aggregates |

Workspace tools accept the same fields as the corresponding CLI request files. Feedback is an agent report, not a compiler or test run. It remains separate from tool executed validation records. Index preparation uses the CLI. There is no MCP install tool or arbitrary SQL query tool.

## Local data and source setup

| Tool | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `workspace_search` | Find workspace files and exact dependency APIs from a question |
| `library_search` | Search a prepared package index |
| `library_symbol` | Inspect an exact API symbol and its relationships |
| `workspace_context` | Resolve imports, definitions and types with your project compiler |
| `workspace_validate` | Compile the project and optionally run an explicit test command |
| `library_feedback` | Record an agent reported query outcome |
| `library_stats` | Inspect local usage and outcome aggregates |

Search, compiler resolution, compilation and execution have separate evidence states. Missing evidence stays visible. [Tool reference](docs/USAGE.md#mcp-tool-reference).

## Your code stays local

Search runs locally. Prepared package indexes work offline. Downloads verify registry integrity and do not run package lifecycle scripts. Indexes and usage records live in `~/.typelatch`; use `TYPELATCH_HOME` to choose another directory or `TYPELATCH_USAGE=off` to disable usage recording.
